terms.comment: Favoured by fortune; the word of greetings and of envy: ō fortūnāte!, lucky you! (fortūnāte senex, Verg. E. 1.46). Traupman’s Valdē fortūnātus es, you’re very lucky (p. 140).
Lucky in what one does, blessed with success, and so also happy (quis mē ūnō vīvit fēlīcior?, Catull. 107.7). Its first sense is fruitful, of trees (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Salvos atque fortūnātus, Eucliō, semper siēs.
phrases.english: May you always be well and fortunate, Euclio.

phrases.latin: ō fortūnātī, quōrum jam moenia surgunt!
phrases.english: how lucky they are, whose walls are already rising!

phrases.latin: Contingit tibi ut aliquot sēdēs vacuae restent.
phrases.english: Lucky for you, there are still some empty seats.
